title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure at the distribution layer rather than a model failure. A fabricated video carried the branding of a news outlet that did not produce it, and the false claim travelled as if it were that outlet's reporting. The account that posted it appeared to be automated, and the reach came from platform distribution rather than from any newsroom.

Catching it required a trademark complaint from the outlet being impersonated, which is a slow, manual route that depends on the target noticing. The platform's own enforcement acted only after that complaint. Nothing in the reporting shows a check at upload time that would have flagged the forged branding or the fabricated payment claim before it accumulated views.

The reporting describes a broader campaign using celebrity deepfakes and false reports impersonating major outlets, and states that the operation had not yet gained major reach. It is not established that the account was a bot, that the network's identity is confirmed beyond the reporting's attribution, or that any named individual or organisation participated in the video's creation.

reports.title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

summary:
A Russian disinformation network known as Storm-1679 or Matryoshka has been spreading fake videos on US social media ahead of the 2026 midterms. One video, falsely branded with a Mother Jones logo, claimed the Democratic National Committee paid $259 million to CNN chief Mark Thompson to promote gender transition among children. It was posted by an X account called роман, which appeared to be a bot, and drew 155,000 views within a day, plus 50,000 more from another account. The campaign also used deepfakes of celebrities like Sarah Jessica Parker and false reports impersonating major news outlets.

After the group @antibot4navalny flagged the video, a lawyer for Mother Jones complained to X, which removed the post for violating its trademark policy. The article says the operation has not yet gained major reach, but warns that Russian influence efforts have targeted every US election since 2016. It notes the Trump administration has closed FBI, intelligence, and State Department units that once tracked foreign disinformation, leaving the US less able to defend against such attacks.
